correctness.rationale: For every derangement each allowed edge has probability exactly 1/(n-1). The integer inequality (-1)^t >= 1-2t is exact for t=0,1, so it yields the lower bound and equality only without co-occurring selected edges. For n>=4 every pair of allowed edges in distinct rows and columns extends to a derangement by a residual Hall perfect matching, forcing all extremizers to be stars. Recurrence parity makes all even-n Walsh coefficients odd; for odd n stars at k=(n-1)/2 exactly cancel and smaller k cannot. Exceptional n=2,3 checked directly. Verified exact two-route checker produced DERANGEMENT_SPARSE_WALSH_PASS with 23,518 cases/groups, not used to infer the theorem.

value.rationale: First vanishing Fourier support weight is a natural robustness and identifiability cutoff for a binary orbit of permutation matrices. A sharp all-n signed lower envelope, full minimizer classification, and exact first-layer zero count constitute a meaningful structural extremal statement, not a finite table lookup. It distinguishes odd-order sparse cancellation from complete invertibility at every even order and directly informs which low-degree Fourier modes are never lost. No unsupported endpoint-stability conclusion is made.
